name: Anthropic Compliance API — Now Covers Cowork and Claude Code Sessions; Beta on Claude Enterprise
hook: Anthropic extended the Compliance API to Claude Cowork (desktop/web/mobile) and Claude Code (CLI + desktop). Security teams can now pull a consolidated server-hosted transcript per session — prompts, responses, tool calls, skill/artifact content, plus verified user ID, org ID, session and per-message IDs — through the same `/v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local` endpoint used for chats today. Additive: nothing changes about existing exports; no separate integration to build if the Compliance API is already enabled. Prior to this, Cowork and Claude Code were the notable audit blind spots for regulated enterprises. Doesn't cover Claude Code on the web, on the Claude Platform, or third-party clouds (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) yet.

name: Claude Cowork in Chrome Side Panel — Skills, Plugins, and Cross-Device Sessions Land in the Extension
hook: Shipped Aug 12: the Claude in Chrome side panel is now a full Claude Cowork session. Configured skills and connectors work inside the browser for the first time; conversations save to your Claude history; and a task started in a Chrome tab (pulling invoices from vendor portals, filling internal dashboards) can continue in Claude Desktop, web, or mobile — and vice versa. Before this, the Chrome panel ran a conversation walled off from the Claude apps. Available today for Max and Team; rolling out to Pro over the coming weeks; Enterprise disabled by default until admins enable it, optionally locked to specific domains. Chrome only for now, no other Chromium browsers or mobile.

name: Claude Code Auto Mode Now Default on Pro, Max, and Team — Permission Prompts Replaced by a Classifier
hook: Starting Aug 14, auto mode became the default permission mode for every new Claude Code session on Pro, Max, and Team plans. Instead of stopping on each tool call, a classifier lets safe actions run and blocks risky ones — the middle ground between approving everything and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Simon Willison flagged a Trajectory Labs eval: 0/720 indirect prompt-injection attempts landed against Fable 5, Opus 5, or Sonnet 5 in auto mode across 72 held-out scenarios. Simon stays on record predicting a coding-agent security incident this year regardless. If you're not on Pro+, or you want the old behavior, set the permission mode explicitly.

name: Claude Code Self-Hosted Environments — Public Beta; Run Cloud Sessions on Your Own Compute
hook: Announced Aug 6, shipped Aug 7 in v2.1.224. One command — `claude self-hosted-runner` — turns your own hosts or containers into the compute layer for Claude Code cloud sessions. Two modes: Fixed (persistent runners) and On-demand (spins up when work queues, shuts down when done). Repo checkouts, build artifacts, secrets, and generated files stay on machines you provision — only prompts/responses/tool results still go to Anthropic's API for inference. Public beta on Team and Enterprise; off by default and not available on ZDR orgs. Pairs with the Compliance API expansion above for a configuration that clears the strictest enterprise reviews.

name: Anthropic Inference Hooks — Webhook DLP Fires Before the Model Sees the Prompt
hook: Shipped Aug 5 in beta for Claude Enterprise. Every governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, and Claude Code (web, desktop, CLI) is sent as a Standard-Webhooks-signed HTTPS POST to your own DLP server, which returns allow/deny (5s timeout) before inference begins. Same check applies to tool responses coming back — including MCP, skills, and plugins. One org-level setting; no proxy, no TLS interception, no endpoint agent. Prod partners at launch: Zscaler, Palo Alto Networks, Netskope, Proofpoint. Prompt-only for now (response-side enforcement is planned); no coverage on Bedrock, Vertex, or voice mode yet.

name: Claude Code v2.1.234–v2.1.235 — Subagent Budget/Concurrency Caps, claude-api Skill Compressed 8×
hook: v2.1.234 (Aug 17) and v2.1.235 (Aug 18) drop concrete guardrails on fan-out: default cap of 20 concurrent subagents (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`), nested-subagent spawning off by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`), and `--max-budget-usd` now actually halts running background subagents once the ceiling is hit — not just new spawns. Bigger cost win: the built-in `claude-api` skill's context load dropped from ~200k+ to ~25k tokens by loading reference docs on demand. Also this window: `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL`, cross-session `notify_when_idle`, `/permissions` and `/add-dir` editable mid-turn, `/goal` auto-checkin after 30+ min waits, spellcheck in the prompt.

name: CVE-2026-54316 — Claude Code's Pre-Approved WebFetch of huggingface.co Weaponized as Exfil Channel; Fixed in 2.1.163
hook: Disclosed at Black Hat USA on Aug 5 by Novee Security. huggingface.co was pre-approved as a bare hostname for the WebFetch tool, so attacker-controlled repos on HF were auto-fetched without a permission prompt and untouched by `--allowedTools`. Attacker instructs Claude to hit `/resolve/main/config.json`-style paths in their own HF repo; HF's public download counter turns into a covert side-channel that leaks env vars, files, and API keys one character at a time. The full chain — starting from a single GitHub issue on a public repo — reached RCE on `anthropics/claude-code` itself and lifted its `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Affects 0.2.54 through 2.1.162; **fixed in 2.1.163**. Anthropic scores it CVSS v4 6.0; NVD 9.1.

name: zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill — ~25.9K Stars, +8K This Week; Client-Neutral Router for Authorized Pentesting
hook: ~25,900 stars — trending trackers logged +8,386 in the past week. A skill router for reverse engineering, authorized penetration testing, and security research: instead of Claude guessing which methodology to apply, 41 routing rules (R0–R40, validated by 163 bilingual regression cases) decide the technique and bootstrap the toolchain on demand. v1.0.1 shipped Aug 8 — refactored routing into a single `skills/config/routing.json` source of truth, added Windows + Ubuntu CI, and unbound it from any one client. Works with Claude Code, Kiro, Cursor, Cline, Codex, and OpenCode. Requires JDK, Node 22.12+, Python 3. MIT.

name: Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts — v2.1.235 Cut Shipped Aug 18; 27 Tools + Subagent Prompts + Token Counts
hook: The most current window into what Claude Code is actually being told, updated within minutes of each release. Current cut: v2.1.235 (Aug 18, 2026). Contains all 27 builtin tool descriptions, the Plan / Explore / Task subagent prompts, and every utility prompt (CLAUDE.md, compact, statusline, magic docs, WebFetch, Bash cmd, security review, agent creation) with per-prompt token counts. CHANGELOG spans 260 versions since v2.0.14 — a June 12 expansion took the tracked prompt count from 350 to 515. Essential for anyone auditing Claude Code behavior, writing a competing harness, or debugging why a tool call reads a certain way. Companion project `tweakcc` lets you override any of these locally.

name: HKUDS/ClawTeam — Multi-Agent Swarm CLI; Leader Agent Spawns Workers in Isolated Worktrees + tmux
hook: 5.5K stars. Framework-agnostic swarm CLI: a leader agent spawns specialized workers, each in its own git worktree and tmux window, and they coordinate through task management, inter-agent messaging, and dependency tracking. Works with any CLI-based agent — Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, nanobot, Cursor. Built-in templates include a hedge-fund team (5 analysts + risk manager + portfolio manager on one command), code-review, and research-paper. One command → full automation. Python 3.10+, tmux, no databases or external services. MIT. Aradotso's trending-skills tracker surfaced it as `clawteam-agent-swarm` this week; win4r's OpenClaw fork adds Windows support via a subprocess backend.

name: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills — ~203K Stars; Day 31; Longest-Running Item in the Digest Window
hook: Day 31 in the digest — passes the one-month mark still in rotation. ~203K stars. A CLAUDE.md encoding Andrej Karpathy's four rules — Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, Goal-Driven Execution — each rule blocking a specific failure mode (unfounded assumptions, unnecessary abstraction, unintended side-effects, vague success criteria). Charlie Automates (@charlieautomates) has been outspoken that the widely-copied 65-line file everyone pastes in isn't Karpathy's own; this repo is Forrest Chang's structured take on the observations. Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 60+ other agents.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 31 — ~203K stars; passes one-month milestone in rotation

name: obra/superpowers — ~272K Stars; Day 9; Full Dev Methodology as Skills
hook: ~272,000 stars — still the most-starred Claude Code skills framework on GitHub. Jesse Vincent (@obra) and Prime Radiant built a complete software-development methodology as chainable skills: brainstorm before you type, plan in bite-sized tasks, enforce TDD (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR), and pass code review before merge. 14+ skills covering the full dev lifecycle; v5.0 added native support for Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI. Accepted into the official Anthropic Claude Code plugin marketplace on January 15, 2026.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — ~99K Stars; Day 26; 65% Fewer Output Tokens; Approaching 100K Milestone
hook: ~99,000 stars — hovering at the 100K milestone. Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing technical accuracy; code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). The /caveman-compress companion shrinks CLAUDE.md and other memory files by ~46%, saving input tokens on every future session permanently.

name: mattpocock/skills — ~220K Stars; Day 2; 21 Engineering Skills From Matt Pocock's Own .agents Directory
hook: Matt Pocock — the TypeScript educator behind Total TypeScript — published his personal .agents directory in March 2026 and it now sits at ~220K stars with 21 composable skills that embed real software-engineering discipline rather than vibe-coding shortcuts. The intended flow: /grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review, with /wayfinder above for multi-session coordination. Star skill: /grill-me — Claude asks every question whose prerequisites are settled in one round, numbers each with a recommended answer, and waits for your input before touching the keyboard. 893K Skillselion installs. MIT. Works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode.

hook: ~127,000 stars. Tauri desktop app managing Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent from a single interface. 50+ provider presets, bidirectional MCP and Skills sync, cloud sync (Dropbox/iCloud/WebDAV), system-tray switching, per-session cost analytics. macOS, Windows, and Linux.
